Year|Bosnian Sportsman of the Year]] (2012) }} }} '''Mirza Teletović''' (born September 18, 1985) is a Bosnian former professional [[basketball]] player who was the president of the [[Basketball Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina]] from 2018 to 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/kosarka/mirza-teletovic-podnio-ostavku-na-mjesto-predsjednika-kosarkaskog-saveza-bih/220608048|title=Mirza Teletović podnio ostavku na mjesto predsjednika Košarkaškog saveza BiH|date=June 8, 2022|access-date=June 8, 2022|language=bs|author=E.B.|publisher=Klix.ba}} As a player, he spent six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represented and [[Captain (sports)|captain]]ed the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national basketball team]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}}, he played at the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. Teletović started his career in Bosnia with [[KK Sloboda Tuzla|Sloboda Tuzla]], which was followed by a stint in Belgium with [[BC Oostende|Oostende]]. He played six years for [[Saski Baskonia]], with whom he won two [[Liga ACB]] championships. He was also named to the [[All-ACB Team]] in 2012. Then, he played five seasons in the NBA for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On September 27, 2018, Teletović announced his retirement after suffering a career-ending [[pulmonary embolism]] injury during his tenure with the Bucks and then got waived in March 2018, removing his final year of his contract in December of that same year. ==Early life== Teletović lived in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] during the [[Bosnian War]] of the 1990s. His parents are from [[Jablanica, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Jablanica]] in the [[Herzegovina]] region. He grew up in [[Mostar]], a city which suffered an [[Siege of Mostar|18-month siege]] when he was a child during the [[Bosnian War]]. When Teletović shared his account of the war, he said:
I was seven years old when the war started. First you start seeing that there's no food, then grenades come down, the whole city is shaking, and you hear people screaming. Every day, your parents come in and say 'our neighbor died, our cousin died'. Always somebody dying. One day, I asked my mother, 'Is anybody alive?' It was very, very rough for us. It left, I will say, a memory...All my friends and me are playing [basketball] and then you hear the sirens like the grenades start falling down and just run to your house and hide. If I have to die, I die. For basketball, I will do anything.{{cite web|title=For Mirza Teletovic, basketball is a game, not war ... and he knows the difference|url=http://www.netsdaily.com/2013/2/16/3996954/for-mirza-teletovic-the-nba-is-game-not-war-and-he-knows-the|work=netsdaily.com|date=16 February 2013|publisher=SBnation}}
As a youth, Teletović spent some of his time playing [[soccer]], as well as learning kickboxing and karate. However, he felt most comfortable with playing basketball, as he played the sport at a local basketball court not far from his home.{{cite web|title=Suns newcomer Teletovic rebounds from adversity|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/09/17/phoenix-suns-mirza-teletovic-rebounds-adversity/72362238/|publisher=[[AZ Central]]|first=Paul|last=Coro|date=September 18, 2015|access-date=September 18, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Mirza Teletovic: Survivor of War, Sickness, and Basketball|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/mirza-teletovic-survivor-war-sickness-and-basketball|work=nba.com/suns|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 17, 2015|access-date=September 17, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Europe=== ====Sloboda Tuzla (2002–2004)==== Teletović made his professional debut with the club [[OKK Sloboda Tuzla|Sloboda Tuzla]], of the [[Basketball Championship of Bosnia and Herzegovina]], during the 2002–03 season. In his first season with the club, he averaged 7.2 points and 2.7 rebounds per game, while in his second season, he increased his stats to 26.4 points and 6.6 rebounds per game over 17 games in the league.{{cite web|title=Mirza Teletovic Draft 2007|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/MirzaTeletovic.html|work=NBA.com|access-date=6 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030083956/http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/MirzaTeletovic.html|archive-date=30 October 2015|url-status=dead}} ====Telindus Oostende (2004–2006)==== In 2004, Teletović moved to the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Belgian Basketball League]] club [[Telindus Oostende]] and stayed for two seasons. He also played in Europe's [[European professional club basketball system|second-tier level]], continental-wide [[Eurocup Basketball|ULEB Cup]] competition, averaging 6.7 points and 2 rebounds. ====Saski Baskonia (2006–2012)==== He joined the [[EuroLeague]] club [[Saski Baskonia]] (known as Tau Cerámica at the time), of the [[Spanish ACB League]], in 2006. He played his first game in the Spanish League on October 1, 2006, in a game against [[Valencia Basket|Pamesa]], where they won on the road by 95–94.{{cite web|title=Spanish League, Game 1: September 30 – October 1, 2006|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/uleb/domestic-leagues/domestic-league-news/i/1164/314/spanish-league-game-1-september-30-october-1-2006|work=Euroleague|access-date=6 June 2012}} In his first season in [[EuroLeague]], Europe's [[European professional club basketball system|first-tier level]], continental-wide competition, he averaged 5.3 points and 2.8 rebounds per game. He declared eligible for the [[2007 NBA draft]], but went [[undrafted]]. In the next three seasons with the Spanish club, he became a starting player, and eventually became the [[captain (sports)|captain]] of Baskonia, and one of the cornerstones of the team. In 2008, he won the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] [[ACB Rising Star Award|Rising Star Award]]. A year later, in 2009, when the club became known as Caja Laboral, he was named the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the mid-season three game [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|Spanish King's Cup]] tournament.{{cite web|title=Teletovic, MVP de la Copa del Rey|url=http://www.libertaddigital.com/deportes/teletovic-mvp-de-la-copa-del-rey-1276351559/|work=Libertad Digital Deportes|date=22 February 2009|access-date=7 June 2012|language=es}} Over 10 games in the [[2011–12 Euroleague|2011–12 Euroleague season]], he averaged a career-high 21.7 points and 6 rebounds per game. However, Caja Laboral did not reach the Top 16 round. In June 2012, Teletović reached a contract buyout agreement with Baskonia, for an amount of €2 million, in order to play the next year in the [[NBA]].{{cite web|title=Caja Laboral and Mirza Teletovic agreed to the NBA buyout amount|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/it/spain/acb/92282/caja-laboral-and-mirza-teletovic-agreed-to-the-nba-buyout-amount.html|work=Sportando|access-date=10 February 2019}} ===NBA=== ====Brooklyn Nets (2012–2015)==== [[file:Mirza Teletovic Nets.jpg|thumb|Teletović with the Nets in March 2013]] On July 16, 2012, Teletović signed a three-year deal with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Mirza Teletovic|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Teletovic_Signing_Release_120711.html|work=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2012|access-date=February 21, 2016}}{{cite web|title=Nets add to roster, bring in European forward Teletovic|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/12/nets-teletovic.ap/index.html|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2012|access-date=February 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504125758/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/12/nets-teletovic.ap/index.html|archive-date=May 4, 2016|url-status=dead}} He made his NBA debut on November 5, 2012, in a game against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On March 1, 2013, Nets head coach [[P. J. Carlesimo]] said that he intended to put Teletović in the Nets rotation, along with giving him consistent minutes.{{cite web|last=Bondy|first=Stefan|title=PJ Carlesimo: Mirza Teletovic "is the biggest piece we have to address."|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/blogs/nets/pj-carlesimo-mirza-teletovic-biggest-piece-address-blog-entry-1.1633240|work=nydailynews.com|date=March 1, 2013|access-date=February 21, 2016}} He went on to tie his season-high of 14 points against the [[Washington Wizards]] in the team's second last game of the season on April 15. He managed just one playoff appearance for the Nets in their 4–3 first round series loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teletmi01/gamelog/2013/ Mirza Teletovic 2012-13 Game Log] On November 29, 2013, Teletović recorded his first career double-double with 18 points and 13 rebounds against the [[Houston Rockets]]. On January 24, 2014, he scored a career-high 34 points in a 107–106 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20140124/DALBKN/gameinfo.html Notebook: Nets 107, Mavericks 106] On February 2, 2014, he recorded his second double-double of the season with 13 points and 11 rebounds against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/teletmi01/gamelog/2014/ Mirza Teletovic 2013-14 Game Log] On December 3, 2014, Teletović scored a season-high 26 points and grabbed a career-high 15 rebounds in a 95–93 overtime win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20141203/SASBKN/gameinfo.html Nets win in OT, snap Spurs' 8-game winning streak] On January 23, 2015, he was ruled out for the rest of the 2014–15 season after he was diagnosed with [[Pulmonary embolism|bilateral pulmonary embolus]].[http://www.nba.com/nets/mirza-teletovic-medical-update-01/23/15 Mirza Teletovic Medical Update - 01/23/15] He made an earlier than expected return for the Nets on April 22, playing four minutes and grabbing two rebounds in Game 2 of the team's first-round series loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150422/BKNATL/gameinfo.html |title=Millsap scores 19, Hawks hold off Nets 96-91 for 2-0 lead |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-04-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150506062321/http://www.nba.com/games/20150422/BKNATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-05-06 |url-status=dead }} On June 18, 2015, the Nets tendered a qualifying offer worth $4.21 million to make Teletović a restricted free agent. However, on July 9, the Nets withdrew their qualifying offer and parted ways with him.[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/07/nets-rescind-qualifying-offer-to-mirza-teletovic.html Nets Rescind Qualifying Offer To Mirza Teletovic] ====Phoenix Suns (2015–2016)==== On July 17, 2015, Teletović signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |date=July 17, 2015 |title=Suns On December 14, 2017, he was sidelined further as a result of [[pulmonary emboli]] in both lungs. Teletović's condition was discovered when consulting with Bucks team physicians after he experienced unusual fatigue earlier in the week.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/medical-update-mirza-teletovic-171214|title=MEDICAL UPDATE ON MIRZA TELETOVIC|work=NBA.com|date=December 14, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2017}} On March 10, 2018, he was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-request-waivers-mirza-teletovic|title=BUCKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON MIRZA TELETOVIC|work=NBA.com|date=March 10, 2018|access-date=March 11, 2018}} On December 21, 2018, the Bucks' request to remove Teletovic's salary from their books for a career-ending injury was granted by the NBA.{{Cite web|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2018/12/24/bucks-get-mirza-teletovics-salary-excluded-from-salary-cap-luxury-tax/|title = Bucks get Mirza Teletovic's salary excluded from salary cap, luxury tax|date = 25 December 2018}} ===Retirement=== On September 27, 2018, Teletović announced his retirement, and revealed that he would start working at the [[Basketball Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina]].{{cite web |title=Teletović potvrdio: Ulazim u KSBiH |url=http://www.bhbasket.ba/teletovic-potvrdio-ulazim-u-ksbih/ |website=BHbasket |access-date=September 27, 2018 |language=bs-BA |date=September 27, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928044000/http://www.bhbasket.ba/teletovic-potvrdio-ulazim-u-ksbih/ |archive-date=September 28, 2018 |url-status=dead }} However, he came out of retirement in 2021 to join local team KK Turbina.{{Cite web |date=2021-09-01 |title=Sport1 - Prije tri godine se oprostio od aktivnog igranja košarke, a sada se vratio iz penzije: Mirza Teletović ima novi klub |url=https://www.oslobodjenje.ba/s1/kosarka/prije-tri-godine-se-oprostio-od-aktivnog-igranja-kosarke-a-sada-se-vratio-iz-penzije-mirza-teletovic-ima-novi-klub-687101 |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=www.oslobodjenje.ba |language=bs-ba}} ==National team career== Teletović played for the national basketball team of [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]]. He has played at the [[EuroBasket 2003]], [[EuroBasket 2005]], [[EuroBasket 2011]], and [[EuroBasket 2013]]. In the EuroBasket 2011 tournament, he averaged 13.8 points and 5.8 rebounds per game; however, Bosnia and Herzegovina finished in 17th place out of 24 teams in the tournament.{{cite web|title=Mirza Teletovic {{!}} EuroBasket 2011|url=http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/cid_4,w7QjPeH-M,ty138LH2l3.playerID_42513.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2011.roundID_7526.teamID_2602.html|work=FIBA Europe|access-date=6 June 2012}} In the [[EuroBasket 2013]] qualification, Teletović averaged 24.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game and helped Bosnia and Herzegovina finished first in group D. During the final tournament, Teletović averaged 21.0 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists per game, with both points and rebounds per game being career highs for Teletović at the EuroBasket. Bosnia and Herzegovina was not able to advance to the second round despite its 3–2 record, leading to a 13th-placed finish.
